one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban opens by recalling that during his 1995-2006 Supreme Court tenure, Valentine's Day at the SC was marked by long-stemmed roses collectively offered by Office of the Clerk of Court staff and by SC Chorale serenades of each justice individually -- and sometimes with their spouses -- in private chambers (one of the few occasions any non-staff visitor was admitted to 'the cloisters in Mount Olympus'), with the ritual softening the yearlong 'monotony of stringency and rigidity' and turning 'judicial frowns into reluctant smiles, even for just a day.' The tradition has since lapsed, and CJ hopes the new SC Ladies Circle under CA Justice Fernanda 'Audrey' Lampas Peralta -- wife of CJ Diosdado M. Peralta -- might revive it or begin a new one. He notes that the Peraltas are only the second appellate judicial love team in Philippine history after the late CJ Ramon C. Aquino and CA Justice Carolina 'Carol' Griño-Aquino (whom CJ retired in 1987 after Corazon Aquino's ascension, with Carol promoted to the SC on Feb 2, 1988), and that since Audrey is only 59 and second-most-senior in the CA after the 'amiable' Justice Remedios A. Salazar Fernando, a promotion within two years would make the Peraltas the only couple to sit on the SC simultaneously. He pivots to the FLP-related news: CJ Peralta's selection board (with PALS chair Joan Sarausos-Largo, TYKF executive Elizabeth Alba, Prof. Tanya Lat, and ADB consultant Joel J. Gregorio) chose 20 Foundation for Liberty and Prosperity / Tan Yan Kee Foundation law scholars for AY 2020 -- 10 named juniors from Ateneo de Manila, Father Saturnino Urios University in Butuan, UST, UP, University of the Cordilleras Baguio, and USC Cebu, and 10 named seniors (one new from FEU and nine retained from the prior year) -- each receiving ₱200,000 (₱100,000 tuition cap, ₱20,000 books, ₱80,000 monthly stipends) on the basis of academic merit and ability to espouse the FLP philosophy of 'liberty and prosperity under the rule of law.' He closes with the FLP Dissertation Writing Contest cosponsored by the Ayala Group: April 30, 2020 deadline, ₱300,000 first prize, ₱200,000 second, three ₱100,000 third places, 20 finalists at ₱20,000 each, with details at www.libpros.com.
